title: Eventual consistency: what the application has to tolerate

videos.script: Eventual consistency sounds like a delay. A value arrives a little late, and then everything is fine. {{delay}} This lesson makes the delay happen, on purpose. A Redis primary, one replica, and a network cable you pull with one command. {{replica}} You write on the primary. You read from the replica. And it answers, with the old value, as if nothing happened. {{stale}} Then the cable comes back, and the copies agree again. That is the eventual part. {{converge}} In between, an application meets three anomalies with names. You do not see your own write. Time seems to run backwards. Two writers overwrite each other. {{anomalies}} Each has a fix the application makes. Read your own writes from the primary. Give every write an id, so a retry is harmless. Put a version number in the document, and update only if it has not moved. {{fixes}} And in Cassandra, the newest timestamp wins. Even when the clock that wrote it was wrong. {{lww}} By the end, a stale read is something you can produce, recognise, and design for.
